stem: A project team needs to select a sub-group of 3 members from a pool of 8 candidates. In how many distinct ways can the sub-group be formed?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Selecting from 9 candidates instead of 8 gives C(9,3) = 84, an off-by-one error in the group size.
Dividing 8 x 7 x 6 = 336 by 2! instead of 3! gives 168; the full factorial of the selection size was not used.
Computing P(8,3) = 8 x 7 x 6 = 336 counts ordered arrangements, not unordered groups.

explanation: Because the sub-group has no internal ordering, use combinations: C(8,3) = 8! / (3! x 5!) = (8 x 7 x 6) / 6 = 56. Dividing by 3! (not 2! or 1!) removes all orderings of the chosen 3 members.
